The lab

One simulated company for all ten projects

Halden Distribution Ltd. (fictional): 85 staff, one head office, one warehouse, 12 remote sales staff. Departments: Management, Finance, HR, Sales, Operations/Warehouse, and IT (me). The situation I inherited: a flat network, shared admin passwords, no MFA, ad-hoc backups nobody has tested, assets tracked in a spreadsheet, tickets arriving by email and WhatsApp, and 30% of PCs on Windows 10.

Every project starts from that inherited state, fixes it, and measures the before/after. The domain is ad.halden.internal — .internal is the top-level domain ICANN reserved for private use in 2024.

Architecture

The whole environment runs as virtual machines on one physical host (Hyper-V on Windows 11 Pro, 16 GB RAM), and it is never exposed to the internet. VMs use dynamic memory and only the ones a phase needs are switched on — that is what keeps ten projects inside 16 GB. In P1 everything sits in one flat 192.168.10.0/24 network; project P6 splits it into the firewall-enforced zones below.

Where the work stands today

Each project is built as a build kit first: the design document, the numbered and idempotent scripts for every phase, the runbooks, the business artifacts and the evidence plan. The build kits for all ten projects exist in therepository.

Lab execution runs phase by phase after that, and that is when the numbers appear here. Until a phase has actually been run, its page shows "not measured" rather than a figure — a deliberate choice, enforced by an automated check that fails the build if a metric has no evidence file behind it.

Tools in the lab

Windows Server 2025 and Windows 11 Enterprise (evaluation), Ubuntu Server 24.04, OPNsense, Hyper-V, Active Directory, Entra ID (trial tenant), PowerShell, Python, Ansible, WSUS, Greenbone Community Edition, Wazuh, Sysmon, GLPI, BookStack, Uptime Kuma, restic, MinIO with Object Lock, Proxmox Backup Server, PingCastle, BloodHound CE, Windows LAPS, HardeningKitty, Atomic Red Team, MITRE ATT&CK Navigator and draw.io. Everything used is free or an evaluation licence.

Honesty statement

This is a home lab: a simulated company, on my own isolated hardware, using evaluation licences and free software. The configurations, scripts and documents are real. The measurements on this site are real measurements — and where a phase has not been run yet, the page says not measured instead of showing a number. Synthetic data (such as the 85-user HR file, the device readiness fleet and the sample vulnerability export) is labelled as synthetic wherever it appears.

The lab is listed on my CV under Projects / Home Lab — never as employment experience — and nothing here was ever run against any network, device or account I do not own. The small number of scripts that simulate attacker behaviour (P3, P7) are written to refuse to run outside the lab and are documented defensively: what was detected and how it was fixed, not how to repeat it.
